display.purpose: The home page's one h1, centred, in two lines.

caption.purpose: The story's one line on the pinned stage, centred, arriving word by word.

caption-still.purpose: The story's five lines in the still layout, in second ink.

page-title.purpose: The h1 of the privacy and not-found pages.

doc-heading.purpose: Headings inside the privacy page's text.

wordmark.purpose: "Trek" beside the mark in the bar and the footer.

title.purpose: A build's name in the builds list.

lede.purpose: The two sentences under the home page's h1.

page-lede.purpose: The sentence under the h1 of the privacy and not-found pages.

button.purpose: Button labels. 17 px on the big button, 14 px on small ones.

compact.purpose: The bar's links and the privacy table. The question card's heading and answers are this size at 500.

label.purpose: The fine line under the button, a build's requirement, a row's second line, the footer.

note.purpose: The line under a capture, the story's staged line and the times in rows.

shadows.name: under-the-inbox-panel
shadows.purpose: A hairline ring and a low, wide shadow under the story's panel of rows. --shade is 40 20 8 on Paper and 0 0 0 at Night.

shadows.name: under-the-phone
shadows.purpose: The shadow under the story's phone, with a faint inner edge on its body.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: The outline of a plain button and of the Deny answer. An outline, not a shadow.

shadows.name: own-build-ring
shadows.purpose: Marks the build that matches the visitor's computer in the builds list.

shadows.name: question-ring
shadows.purpose: The outline of the question card.

motion.name: out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--out): entrances, hovers, presses, the captions' words and the rows' glide.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Colour and underline changes under the pointer.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A button scaling to 0.98 while pressed.

motion.name: entrance-rise
motion.purpose: The first screen's headline, lede, button and fine line on load: opacity, a 14px rise and an 8px blur that clears. CSS, so it runs without the script. Off with Reduce Motion.

motion.name: story-scroll
motion.purpose: The pinned story. Scrolling plays its five moments forwards and backwards. The played position moves 16% of the way to the scroll position each frame.

motion.name: caption-word
motion.value: 520ms in, 55ms between words, the first 170ms after the change; 180ms out
motion.purpose: A caption arriving word by word: opacity, a 10px rise and a 9px blur that clears. A line's words leave together.

motion.name: row-arrival
motion.purpose: The rows gathering as the stage comes up the screen: opacity, a 26px rise and a 7px blur that clears, each row starting after the one above it.

motion.name: row-glide
motion.purpose: A row moving to its new place when the order changes.

motion.name: row-state
motion.purpose: A row's wash and its dot changing colour.

motion.name: question-card
motion.purpose: The question card coming and going: opacity, a 10px rise and a 6px blur.

motion.name: allow-press
motion.purpose: Going forward into "It gets back to work.": Allow scales to 0.95 and goes to accent-over, and the stage settles 220ms after the press.

motion.name: phone
motion.value: tied to scroll: in from 40% to 47%, out from 58% to 63%
motion.purpose: The phone coming up beside the block: opacity, a 70px rise and a 4 degree turn that straightens. Under 1000px wide it rises 60px over the block and does not turn.

motion.name: ring-turn
motion.purpose: The ring of a thread at work. Off with Reduce Motion.

motion.name: hiker-clock
motion.purpose: The hiker's walk, as in the app: 16 art pixels a second, 0.35s to gather and lose speed, a pose every 4 pixels, a 1.2s rest and a turn at each end. Time moves him and scroll never sets his place. Runs while the trail is on screen and the tab is in front. Off with Reduce Motion.

motion.name: fit
motion.purpose: The stage's block shrinking from its top centre to fit a short window (--k), so it never meets the caption. The hiker's cell follows the scale, so one art pixel stays a whole number of device pixels.

motion.name: still
motion.value: no script, Reduce Motion, or a window under 560px tall
motion.purpose: The story as a still layout: the asking moment, the phone under it, all five captions and the staged line. Not pinned.

narrative.overview:
The site is where a visitor meets Trek before installing it. The first screen is one photograph of a trail going up a dry hill. A headline, two short sentences, one button and one fine line sit in its sky. Below the photograph the page takes the app's own ground: Paper by day, Night when the system is dark.

Under the first screen the page shows the app three times. First a small stage is pinned while the visitor scrolls, and an example Inbox acts on it: three threads start, one stops to ask, the phone offers the same question, the thread goes back to work, finished work waits. Then the real window is shown at its real size, twice. A list of builds and a one-line footer end the page.

Type is two grotesques, upright throughout. Surfaces are flat, with hairlines and small steps in tone. The page draws two soft shadows, both on the stage. Decorative art is a photograph or it is absent. There is no drawn scenery, and the mark is never used as scenery. The home page does not use a dark page by default, a shrunken window under the headline, a row of agent logos or a wall of copy.

Motion has one grammar. Things arrive by opacity and a short rise, most with a blur that clears. Scrolling plays the stage forwards and backwards. The hiker walks on a clock. Without the script, with Reduce Motion on, or in a window under 560 px tall, the story is a still layout that says the same things.
keyCharacteristics: Paper by default and Night when the system is dark. There is no switch on the page.
One photograph on the first screen: the day picture on Paper, a dusk grade of the same frame at Night.
One accent, ember, for the action and for a thread at work. Amber and emerald mark the other two states.
Bricolage Grotesque at 600 for display, Hanken Grotesk at 400 and 500 for text, JetBrains Mono for commands.
A pinned story 430vh tall, with one caption on screen at a time.
Two window captures at one CSS pixel to the point. One reduced capture, the story's iPhone.
The 12 by 16 pixel hiker on a dotted trail, in the story only, in the app's own timing.
Flat surfaces, hairlines, and corners of 10 to 18 px.
No trackers, analytics or third-party fonts. One request leaves the page, to GitHub's API for the latest release.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: In what the page itself draws, colour beyond ink and paper belongs to two things: the action (the filled button, Allow, the ring on the visitor's own build, the focus outline) and a thread's state (ember at work, amber waiting, emerald finished). The pictures bring their own colour: the photograph, the mark, the hiker's pack.

rules.name: The Two Themes Rule
rules.body: The page has the app's two themes and no others: Paper by day and Night when the system is dark. Every colour is defined in both, and every picture ships in both.

rules.name: The State Ink Rule
rules.body: On Paper a state's words use its ink shade, because the dot's colour is too light for text. At Night the dot's colour serves for both.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Display type is Bricolage Grotesque at 600. A headline's weight stays between 500 and 700, and a light weight is never used. The wordmark, at 500, is the only other display weight on the site.

rules.name: The Upright Rule
rules.body: There are no italics. No italic file is shipped and the browser is told not to make one.

rules.name: The Plain Headline Rule
rules.body: A headline is a plain statement in one colour. On the home page each headline and each caption ends with a full stop. Nothing sits above a headline: no label and no pill. Display copy has no colon and no semicolon. No paragraph of copy opens with a bold lead-in. The example row's "Waiting: run ./migrate?" is the app's own wording and is not display copy.

rules.name: The Real Size Rule
rules.body: A window capture is set at one CSS pixel to the point: a 2x file at half its pixel size. On a screen too narrow for it the picture is cropped to the part that makes the point. It is never scaled down.

rules.name: The One Reduced Capture Rule
rules.body: The story's iPhone is the one capture that is not at real size. It is a prop beside the stage, not a product shot. Its screen is 169 px wide on the stage and 194 px wide in the still layout, against the phone's 390 points.

rules.name: The Few Pictures Rule
rules.body: The home page has one photograph, two captures of the app's window and one reduced iPhone capture. No section holds more than one.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: The page draws two soft shadows, under the Inbox panel and under the phone. Everything else is flat: a hairline or a step in tone.

rules.name: The Story Only Rule
rules.body: The hiker walks on the story's dotted trail and nowhere else. He is never in the first screen.

rules.name: The Clock Not Scroll Rule
rules.body: Time moves the hiker. Scroll starts and stops his clock and never sets his place.

rules.name: The No Pause Button Rule
rules.body: The hiker has no control beside him. Pressing the hiker stops him, and pressing him again sends him on.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: On the pinned stage one caption is on screen at a time, and it arrives word by word.

rules.name: The Photograph Or Nothing Rule
rules.body: Decorative art is a photograph or it is absent. The hiker and his dotted trail are the app's own working animation, not scenery.

rules.name: The Mark Is Not Scenery Rule
rules.body: The mark is a logo beside the name and an icon. It is never enlarged, repeated or laid behind anything.

rules.name: The Staged Is Said Rule
rules.body: A capture or an example with staged content says so in a visible line under it.

rules.name: The Reads Whole Rule
rules.body: Without the script, with Reduce Motion on, and in a short window, every word, picture and link is still there and still true: the story is the still layout, the hiker stands or walks his trail, and every download link leads to the latest release.

dos: Do set display type in Bricolage Grotesque at 600, upright, in one colour, and end a home-page headline with a full stop.
Do use a photograph for decorative art, or use nothing.
Do show a window capture at real size, a 2x file at half its pixel size, and crop it on a narrow screen.
Do ship every picture in Paper and in Night, and define every colour in both.
Do say in a visible line under a capture or an example when its content is staged.
Do keep the hiker on the story's dotted trail, on his own clock.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better against its ground. On Paper, write a state in its ink shade.
Do keep the page whole without its script, with Reduce Motion on, and in a short window.
Do keep the site's words few, and within what the repository's README says.
Do write the origin of every new or retaken picture into the file or into the `.json` file beside it.
Do check a new mark against competitors' marks and popular app icons before it is shown.
Do serve type, pictures and script from this domain. The only request elsewhere is to GitHub's API for the latest release.
donts: Don't put the hiker in the first screen, or anywhere but the story.
Don't add a pause button for the hiker. Pressing the hiker stops him.
Don't set the hiker's place by scroll.
Don't use the mark as scenery.
Don't use a letter as the mark.
Don't make the mark an orange tile with a white figure.
Don't copy a competitor's site or mark, or leave room for anyone to say so.
Don't set a headline lighter than 500 or heavier than 700.
Don't use italics, bold lead-ins, a two-tone headline, or a pill or label above a headline.
Don't use a colon or a semicolon in display copy, or write a balanced "X, and Y" line. The copy must not read as machine-written.
